sn10.12:1.2: Another spirit of place, Āḷavaka’s story (also at [snp1.10]()) is perhaps the most beloved of all the _yakkha_ conversions. He is provided with an extensive backstory in the Pali commentaries, and another quite different story in a Chinese Dharmapada (T 211, pp. 575–609). | Āḷavī was a town between Sāvatthī and Rājagaha.
sn10.12:9.2: Following Cone’s *Dictionary of Pali*, Pali _gharamesin_ probably stands for Sanskrit _gṛhamedhin_, an “householder of discernment”, a man of mature years who has completed his education.
sn10.12:10.4: Readings are uncertain. Chinese parallels at SA2 325 and SA 1326 support _dama_ or _danta_ here rather than _dhamma_. [dn30:1.6.2]() has both, and elsewhere we find both _dhamma_ and _dama_ commonly used alongside _sacca_.
